topic: Zoro figuring out how to kill a Knight of God in 1193 and 1194 shows Imu's guardians are not immortal
title: Why Knights Of God Can Finally Die (One Piece 1194)
description: Chapter 1193 and 1194 quietly answered a question fans asked for years: how do you kill a Knight of God? Here is what Sommers' fight really showed, and why Imu's guards may not be untouchable anymore. Do you agree?
comment: Imu's Knights of God: do they now have a real weakness, or will Imu just replace them? Pick one.

lines.text: Knights of God can die. Chapter 1194 just proved it.

shot.fallback: armored holy knight with a steel body

lines.text: For years, fans asked how you even hurt these guys.

shot.fallback: group of armored knights on a stone hall

lines.text: Sommers kept regenerating, no matter how many times Zoro cut him.
Then in chapter 1193, Zoro figured out the rule.
Only a Supreme King Haki strike to the steel heart finishes a Knight of God.

shot.fallback: three swords crackling with black lightning
swordsman gripping three swords in a storm

lines.text: Zoro coats all three swords, and Sommers stops regenerating.

shot.fallback: three swords wrapped in black lightning and flame

lines.text: Here's what nobody's talking about. That's a repeatable method, not a lucky hit.
People say Imu will just possess someone else and keep going.

shot.fallback: shadowy figure controlling a woman with dark eyes

lines.text: True, Imu took over Gunko and turned Dorry and Brogy with Domi Reversi.

shot.fallback: giant warriors with hollow dark eyes

lines.text: But every guard Imu spends is one guard the world can now actually kill.

shot.fallback: shadowy ruler on a throne with empty seats

lines.text: That's my read: Imu isn't losing power yet, but the wall just got a crack.
And it started with a swordsman who cut what couldn't die. Knights of God can die.

shot.fallback: swordsman standing over a fallen knight
